sections.h2: What kind of housing market is Coconut Creek in Broward County?
sections.html: Coconut Creek is a Broward County city with 58,626 residents on the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate, up from 52,909 in 2010 and 57,833 in 2020. It is compact: 11.17 square miles of land held roughly 5,179 residents per square mile when the 2020 Census was taken. Check whether your home belongs to a homeowner or condominium association, since the vacation rental affidavit on the city's site refers to notice to a mandatory association and its rules can add steps to a sale.

sections.h2: What housing figures does the Census report for Coconut Creek?
sections.html:
A typical owner-occupied Coconut Creek home was valued at $309,600 for 2020 through 2024, and 64.8% of housing is lived in by its owner. Rent at the midpoint is $2,102 a month, so owners of rental units can compare that income with what a sale would bring.

  • Households: 24,304, with 2.39 people each.
  • Monthly owner costs: $2,162 with a mortgage, $890 without.
  • Foreign-born residents: 33.0%; another language spoken at home: 39.6%.
  • Age 65 or older: 20.1%; under 18: 21.8%.
  • Travel time to work: 29.6 minutes.

Because 39.6% of residents use another language at home, read every contract and disclosure in full and ask for a translation if you need one.

sections.h2: Does Coconut Creek allow vacation rentals, and does that matter for a sale?
sections.html:
Yes. The city's vacation rental page says its regulations do not prohibit vacation rentals or limit how long or how often a home is rented. They exist to protect neighborhoods and life safety, and every vacation rental must register and obtain a Vacation Rental Certification.

If you hold one, tell buyers up front. A certification is part of the property's income story, and a buyer who wants it has to file a new application. The city lists these details:

  • Application or registration fee: $250. Renewal: $250. Re-inspection: $40.
  • Registrations expire annually and must be renewed before September 30.
  • Fire safety and code compliance inspections come before the first certificate, under Ordinance No. 2021-003, by appointment.
  • Packet items: a Florida DBPR transient public lodging license, Florida Department of Revenue sales tax registration, a Broward County business tax receipt and Broward tourist development tax registration.

The city page also gives a notarized-letter option for owners whose booking sites collect taxes. Ask the city's business tax office for the current form.

sections.h2: What should a Coconut Creek landlord do before selling a rented house?
sections.html:
Read the lease first. Florida needs at least 30 days of notice to end a tenancy that renews monthly, and a tenant behind on rent is owed 3 days of written notice that excludes weekends and court holidays. Florida's eviction statute lays out the notice and the court steps, so follow them if a tenant must leave before closing.

Selling with the tenant staying means the rent keeps flowing and no gap opens between occupants. Put the lease, security deposit amount and rent ledger in the contract package.

sections.h2: How does Broward treat deed tax on a Coconut Creek sale?
sections.html:
In Broward the deed tax is the statewide 70 cents per $100 of price. Only Miami-Dade differs. The tax covers any mortgage or encumbrance on the property whether or not the buyer takes it over, every person on the deed answers for it regardless of what the contract says, and the Broward clerk collects it at recording.

Statutory recording charges are separate: a first page costs $5.00 and later pages are $4.00 apiece, plus other per-page fees. Have the closing agent list each one.

sections.h2: How do Broward homestead and property tax dates affect a Coconut Creek sale?
sections.html:
The assessment date for every parcel is January 1. A homestead exemption of up to $50,000 needs an application by March 1 and proof that you made the home your permanent residence by January 1. The first $25,000 reaches every tax; the second $25,000 applies only above $50,000 of value and only to non-school taxes.

Save Our Homes holds yearly growth in assessed value to 3 percent or inflation, whichever is lower. The sale itself resets the parcel to just value on the following January 1. Bills arrive each November with discounts that shrink from 4 percent to 1 percent by February, and April 1 is the delinquency date. A mid-year closing means the title company divides the tax with the buyer.

sections.h2: What if a Coconut Creek owner faces foreclosure or an inherited house?
sections.html:
Foreclosure here is a court matter. The clerk holds the auction within a window of 20 to 35 days after final judgment, longer if the lender consents. If the house sells first, the lender is paid from the proceeds. If the house came from an estate, a non-exempt estate of $150,000 or less can use summary administration, as can an estate where more than two years have gone by since the death.

Either case rewards an early call to the servicer, a Florida attorney or the probate clerk. A cash buyer can work around those dates, yet the court sets the schedule.

sections.h2: What if property taxes on a Coconut Creek house go unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquency starts April 1. The tax collector then sells certificates on the unpaid bills by June 1, and bidders offer the lowest interest rate they will accept, in quarter-point steps. The certificate holder may not ask the owner for money until two years after April 1 of the issue year.

Once two years pass, the holder can request a tax deed for a $75 application fee, and the clerk conducts the auction. A homestead's opening bid includes half of its assessed value. Back taxes can be cleared from proceeds at closing; request the payoff figure from the title company.

sections.h2: Which Florida tax breaks might apply to a Coconut Creek owner?
sections.html:
Owners 65 or older may get another homestead exemption of up to $50,000 where a local ordinance allows it and household income stays under the limit. A 10 percent or greater disability, with an honorable discharge and Florida residency, brings a $5,000 cut in assessed value. Total and permanent service-connected disability can qualify for a full homestead exemption. The Census counts 1,850 veterans in Coconut Creek, so these rules reach real owners here.

Homestead ends when you rent the home or move out, though a servicemember may rent without losing it. Ask the Broward property appraiser which exemptions sit on your parcel before closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Coconut Creek house that has a vacation rental certification?
faqs.a: Yes. The certification belongs to the current owner, and a buyer planning short-term stays has to register separately. Check the city's annual September 30 renewal date and your fee status before closing.

faqs.q: Do I owe the city anything before I sell my Coconut Creek home?
faqs.a: Ask the city's Building Division about open permits and the code office about open violations, since either can hold up closing.

faqs.q: How fast can a cash sale close in Coconut Creek?
faqs.a: HOA approval, title work and any lien payoffs can still add days.

faqs.q: Who pays Broward deed tax on a sale in Coconut Creek?
faqs.a: The state holds every person on the deed liable, and contracts typically assign it to the seller. The deed tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration.

faqs.q: What happens to my Coconut Creek tenant if the house sells?
faqs.a: The lease generally carries on unless it ends or the proper notice is served. Florida requires at least 30 days of notice for a tenant renewing monthly.
